newsitem.title: INDIA: India to decide oil price hike next week - PM.
newsitem.headline: India to decide oil price hike next week - PM.

text.p: The decision-making Steering Committee of India's ruling United Front will meet on June 8 to reach a consensus on increasing oil prices, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Saturday.
"There are four or five options to tackle the oil pool deficit," Gujral told reporters before leaving for New Delhi after a day-long visit to Bombay.
He said the committee will consider these options and would have to arrive at a consensus decision at their June 8 meeting.
The 15-party minority government's decision-making committee at a meeting last Sunday failed to arrive at a decision to raise government-set prices as left parties resisted the move.
The front's left-wing partners favour increasing crude oil production and cutting import duties on crude oil and petroleum products instead of raising oil prices.
Gujral said he would present the options to the committee.
Both Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have said the government must soon decide how to repay money it owes to oil companies for selling petroleum products at well below global prices.

The outstanding amount, called the oil pool deficit, totalled 155 billion rupees ($4.33 billion) at the end of March 1997 and is expected to rise to 245 billion rupees by March 31, 1998, according to government figures.
